findings.title: Exact-model conditional relied on the top-level required list
findings.body: Round 1 flagged that the gemini-3.1-pro-high if/then clause could pass vacuously when auditor_tool is absent, since JSON Schema properties is vacuous for a missing key. The risk was not reachable: auditor_tool is in the schema's top-level required array. It was closed directly anyway by adding "required": ["auditor_tool"] to the then clause, making the conditional self-contained. Strict tightening; no proof that validated before changes verdict. Covered by tests/audit/test_agy_gemini31_model.py::test_exact_model_requires_auditor_tool_to_be_present. Round 2 Q1/Q10(a) and round 3 Q2: PASS.

findings.title: Round 1 was asked to verify the auditor report inside the tree it was auditing
findings.body: Producer prompt-scope defect, not a change defect. The canonical AUDITOR_REPORT.md is the audit's own output and cannot exist in the audited tree. The placement is forced: the trusted schema requires report_path under a single proof/ directory, while proof-only closure confines the successor commit to proof/pr_merge/embedded-audit/pr-1165/. Rounds 2 and 3 were given the ordering constraint and instructed to flag any file claiming the report already existed; neither found one. Disclosed in the report. Round 2 Q6/Q10(b): PASS.

findings.title: Claimed unauthorized addition of pal-mcp-clink to the auditor_tool enum
findings.body: Refuted. pal-mcp-clink is already present in the trusted schema on main at 5d694cc9898e5046b5da03319f20f48599c40ca8; this change does not touch the auditor_tool enum. The documentation line had omitted it and the diff corrects that omission, now stated explicitly in docs/ops/embedded-audit-proof.md. Round 1 saw only the diff, not main, so it could not distinguish documentation catch-up from an enum addition. Round 2, shown the full schema hunk, confirmed the enum is untouched. Round 2 Q10(c): PASS.

findings.title: Trusted local-attestation route did not enforce the canonical schema's conditionals
findings.body: Found by reviewer after round 2 passed. scripts/audit/local_audit_acceptance.py validated the signed embedded_audit with a hand-rolled stdlib check of required keys, a few enum memberships and a few types. It never walked allOf, so no schema conditional was enforced on the signed route, and it exempted report_path outright. Reproduced before repair: the fixture {status PASS, auditor_model gemini-3.1-pro-high, auditor_tool claude-code-cli} was ACCEPTED by the origin/main acceptance route while the canonical Draft7Validator rejected it with 'agy' was expected. The defect sat behind the signature trust boundary, so it let a trusted signer record a forbidden pairing rather than letting an untrusted party in; it is nonetheless disqualifying for a PR whose purpose is an exact model-to-tool trust contract. Repaired by executing the canonical schema with real Draft 7 semantics on both validation routes, with no second hand-written validator. Both paths now reject the fixture. Evidence: review_bundle/DEFECT_REPRODUCTION_ROUND3.txt. Round 3 Q1-Q3, Q5, Q7-Q8: PASS.

fixes_applied: Replaced the partial hand-rolled structural check in scripts/audit/local_audit_acceptance.py with canonical Draft 7 execution against the trusted schema, so allOf conditionals, additionalProperties and report_path are all enforced and a future schema conditional needs no second implementation.
Removed the report_path validation exemption and the docstrings promising it; a downstream emitter substituting its own path is not a reason to accept a schema-invalid signed input.
Kept verdict policy separate from schema validity, since the trusted schema admits FAIL and SKIPPED for CI diagnostic proofs while local attestation accepts passing verdicts only.

Made the acceptance route fail closed with schema_validator_unavailable when jsonschema is absent, with no fallback to a partial check, and provisioned the validator explicitly in the embedded-audit workflow so a trust gate does not depend on an undeclared runner-image package.
Added a parity fixture corpus asserting the acceptance route and Draft7Validator agree, an end-to-end wrong-tool rejection test, and a guard that fails when a new schema conditional lacks coverage.
Corrected the acceptance test fixture, which itself encoded a schema-invalid two-directory report_path — which is why the exemption had looked safe.
Added "required": ["auditor_tool"] to the gemini-3.1-pro-high conditional's then clause so it cannot pass vacuously, with a regression test.
Stated in docs/ops/embedded-audit-proof.md that pal-mcp-clink was already present in the trusted schema on main and is documentation catch-up, not an enum addition.
Moved the canonical auditor report to proof/TP-DMX-AUDIT-AGY-GEMINI31-APPROVAL-001-REPAIR-001/AUDITOR_REPORT.md so report_path satisfies the trusted schema pattern.
Recorded the schema evidence boundary as ACCEPTED_DESIGN_BOUNDARY in docs and pinned it with a characterisation test.
Filed TP-DMX-EMBEDDED-AUDIT-VALIDATOR-SCOPE-PARITY-001 for the separate sweep and pre-commit scope gap, which this repair does not close.
remaining_risks: provider_attested is false: the exact selector gemini-3.1-pro-high is established by local AGY CLI evidence (v1.1.11 model list, fail-closed rejection of an unknown selector) and by the recorded invocation, not by a credentialed provider attestation. No hosted credential was added and none is claimed.

Bootstrap representation: auditor_model is recorded as the generic 'gemini' because gemini-3.1-pro-high is absent from origin/main:schemas/proof/embedded_audit.schema.json at 5d694cc9898e5046b5da03319f20f48599c40ca8. The new enum value does not bootstrap its own admission; exact-selector truth is carried by the invocation and the auditor report.

The JSON Schema binds the declared tool/model pair only and deliberately does not parse invocation, so schema validity is not evidence of runtime selector execution. Recorded as ACCEPTED_DESIGN_BOUNDARY: SCHEMA_BINDS_DECLARED_TOOL_MODEL_PAIR; RUNTIME_SELECTOR_PROVEN_BY_EXECUTION_EVIDENCE.

Confirmed and still open: proof/.validator_scope.json includes only proof/TP-DMX-*/PROOF.json and skips proof/pr_merge/** under default_when_unmatched skip_with_warning, and the pre-commit proof hook has the same blind spot via files ^proof/[^/]+/PROOF\.json$. Repairing local_audit_acceptance.py closes the signed local-attestation route only and does NOT close the sweep or pre-commit gap; observed again this cycle, the pre-commit proof hook reported no files to check while this proof was in the diff. This proof is validated by a direct scripts/audit/validate_audit_proof.py run instead. Filed as TP-DMX-EMBEDDED-AUDIT-VALIDATOR-SCOPE-PARITY-001.

The workflow now installs jsonschema at job runtime. Because embedded-audit runs on pull_request_target, both the workflow and the acceptance script are taken from the trusted base ref, so this provisioning is inert for PR #1165's own CI and is first exercised after merge. Until then the acceptance route in CI is main's pre-repair version.

The audited head 9b901093e441a709d8c31e1067d5745a1604112f adds the audit's own outputs on top of the tree AGY reviewed (d2d3ff808e80e6d6a490616d4ff2341a63c29d86). The delta is only AUDITOR_REPORT.md, the raw round-3 transcript, the defect reproduction, and runner-evidence captures under review_bundle/; no schema, validator, test, packet, documentation, or workflow byte changed after the audit. This ordering is forced and is disclosed rather than left implicit.
